opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, maximum is write (admin requires owning role; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code). Requested level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E024 (Donna Ball) as contractor with basic training (note: HR listed full_time). Contractors max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds policy. Recommend read.
reason: E024 (Donna Ball) requests write access to Source Code. The HR note lists her as full-time (max write), but the Security agent's own database lookup lists her employment type as contractor with basic security training, explicitly flagging the discrepancy with HR. Under policy, contractor employees without advanced security training have a maximum of read on Source Code (admin/write beyond read not permitted). Since the requested write exceeds the contractor maximum of read, the maximum (read) is granted. Granting the more restrictive level is consistent with the policy using the verified security data.
